summary: 2026-09-27 17:00 PDT (-0700), measured by running `date` this turn. I checked the diff against `reviews/refusal-diagnostics.md` criterion by criterion and found no correctness defect: the three quotation-refusal sites (the opening's `verifyQuotations` check, the mid-answer `verifyQuotedSpan` check, and the mid-answer grammar `violation` token) all now funnel through `refuseQuotation` → `stopper`, so no path keeps the old 60-character line (AC2, R5); `refusalEntry` logs the whole quotation when its first `REFUSAL_OPENING_CHARS` characters are found in a retrieved passage and otherwise keeps exactly that opening with `shortened` naming the full length and the reason (AC1, AC7, option B); `verifyQuotedSpan` now reports `candidates` — the documents it actually tested — as a required `citedAs` list, `[]` for `no-citation`, `elided` and grammar violations (AC3, AC4); the record is `JSON.stringify`d at the single call site so it reaches the console as one unbroken string (AC4 of the story's in-scope list); the reader path is untouched, still receiving only `PROVENANCE_NOTICE` (AC6); and the README section matches the four fields the code emits (AC8). I verified the arithmetic the AC1/AC7 tests rest on (the 16,000-character quotation is genuinely past the console's 10,000-character cut, opens in the passage, and normalises to itself), that the test fingerprints do not collide with `PROVENANCE_NOTICE`, that the exhaustively-keyed reason fixture really does fail the typecheck when a reason is added, and that no consumer outside `src/lib/voice.ts` and the tests reads `citedAs`, so widening it from `string?` to `readonly string[]` breaks nothing else. The hidden-failure lens is clean here too: no blind catch, silent fallback, or removed assertion is introduced, and `refusalEntry` has no error path that could swallow a refusal. What remains are two documentation-precision nits below; nothing blocks.

findings.title: The README identifies the refusal entry by a log label that also carries a non-JSON line
findings.claim: The new section says the refusal's entry is "labelled `answer refused on provenance`, holding one JSON object", and introduces the field table from that label. The label is not unique to quotation refusals: `stop` (src/lib/chat/orchestrate.ts:363) is also used by `refuseImpersonation` (src/lib/chat/orchestrate.ts:381-382), which logs the free text `opening impersonated ("…") …` under the same label — deliberately, per the story's non-goal that an impersonating opening keeps its current log line. An operator who greps the label to diagnose a live refusal can therefore land on a line that is not JSON and has none of the four documented fields, which is the opposite of the story's stated purpose for the README passage. The README's own sentence is scoped to "the quotation screen refuses a quotation", so this is a precision gap rather than a false claim, and AC8's reviewer oracle does not name it as a red — hence NIT, not IMPORTANT.
findings.suggestion: Either scope the claim to the entry's shape rather than its label ("a quotation refusal's entry holds one JSON object with these fields") or say plainly that the label is shared and that `check`/`quotation` distinguish a quotation refusal's JSON record from the impersonating-opening line.

findings.title: `stop` keeps a free-text seam, so the story's "structural" R5 mitigation is an assertion rather than an enforcement
findings.claim: The comment on `stop` states the guarantee "Called only through the two refusals below, so a quotation refusal cannot log anything but its record", and the story's regressions table relies on the same reasoning ("The mitigation is structural: the free-text refusal is narrowed to the impersonating opening, so a new quotation refusal has to build the record"). In fact `stop` takes an untyped `string` and is a free-text helper of exactly the shape of the `refuse(why: string)` it replaced — the old helper was removed, but its capability moved here under a new name. The guarantee therefore holds only by convention: a future refusal site can call `stop` with a hand-built 60-character line and nothing in the types or the tests stops it, which is precisely the stated R5 gap. No current behaviour is wrong, so this is a NIT.
findings.suggestion: Either make the guarantee real — have `stop` accept the record (serialising it inside) so the only free text a call site can supply is the impersonation form — or soften the comment to state what is true of today's call sites ("the quotation refusals below all log `refusalEntry`'s record") so it is not read as an enforced invariant.
